title: Taro Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Taro Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Taro nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, potassium and phosphorus in gabi, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Taro nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your gabi (taro) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus, calcium, magnesium, sulfur, iron and zinc. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Taro leaf scorched brown along the edges and between the veins from potassium shortage
heroImage.credit: Scot Nelson (photo by Douglas Hunefeld Photograph), CC0 1.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But calcium, sulfur, iron and zinc stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which taro nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.
Taro nutrient deficiency signs, old leaves and young leaves
Shows first on the old leaves

blocks.text: Shows first on the young leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the young leaves of gabi

The youngest leaf yellows between the veins and cups, with brown edges, and roots die back.

Plants are just stunted with small leaves. There are few other signs.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a taro nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest taro nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in taro

Roots, main shoot and suckers stay stunted. Yellowing starts on the oldest leaf blades and, as it gets worse, all the blades turn yellow. Old leaves die early, so fewer leaves are working and the corm yield drops. You see it most at this stage: from 2 months after planting through corm bulking.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in gabi
Flooded (wetland) taro loses nitrogen to the air when the soil has no oxygen. Taro grows best when soil nitrogen is mostly in the nitrate form.
How to tell it apart

Sulfur deficiency yellows the young leaves evenly. Magnesium deficiency yellows between the veins of old leaves. To be sure, leaf test of leaf number 2 (the second fully opened leaf below the newest one): below 4.0 percent nitrogen is deficient (CTAHR).
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Apply nitrogen following the soil test, for example Urea 46 0 0 or Complete 14 14 14 in split doses. You can also give a urea spray of 10 g per liter every 15 days. Do not overdo it: too much nitrogen promotes taro leaf blight (CTAHR).

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, split nitrogen through the season and add compost or manure.
Potassium deficiency in taro

blocks.alt: Taro leaf scorched brown along the edges and between the veins from potassium shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Scot Nelson (photo by Douglas Hunefeld Photograph), CC0 1.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Growth slows, plants wilt easily and leaf blades are smaller. Older leaves get a burnt look between the veins or along the edges. In some varieties irregular brown spots form in the center of older blades and join until the whole leaf yellows or browns. Corms stay small. You see it most at this stage: corm bulking.
Why potassium deficiency happens in gabi
Sandy and leached soils, and fields where taro and other root crops have been grown for years.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency yellows between veins first, then browns the margins. Taro leaf blight gives water soaked spots that ooze, mainly in wet weather. To be sure, leaf test of leaf number 2. Soil test for potassium.
What to apply for potassium deficiency
Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 following the soil test, split in parts. Give a potassium sulfate spray of 10 g per liter as a quick fix.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, return crop waste and add wood ash or compost.
Phosphorus deficiency in taro

Root and shoot growth are stunted. Older leaf blades can look darker green, and in some varieties many light colored dots form between the veins. Later the leaf edges yellow and turn brown. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in gabi
Acid upland soils and volcanic soils that hold phosphorus. In flooded fields phosphorus becomes more available.
How to tell it apart
Potassium deficiency gives brown spots and scorched edges, not light dots on dark leaves. To be sure, leaf test (0.3 to 0.5 percent phosphorus is sufficient, CTAHR) and a soil test.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency
Use single superphosphate for a quick fix and rock phosphate for the long term, following the soil test.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, apply phosphorus at planting and add organic manure.
Calcium deficiency in taro

Root and shoot growth drop and roots look stunted. The youngest leaf blade first yellows between the veins. In severe cases blades cup, with brown edges, then fail to unfurl and the shoot dies. Dying roots let soil diseases in. You see it most at this stage: early growth, on acid upland soils.
Why calcium deficiency happens in gabi
Very acid soils. At pH 4 aluminum also poisons the roots (CTAHR).
How to tell it apart

Manganese toxicity in older leaves can look like calcium deficiency with cupped blades. Calcium deficiency starts on the youngest leaf. To be sure, leaf test (below 0.7 percent calcium is deficient, CTAHR) and a soil pH test.
What to apply for calcium deficiency
On acid soils, lime about 250 kg per hectare where the pH is 5.5 to 6. About 840 kg per hectare in two splits where it is 3.5 to 4.5. CTAHR found dolomite protected taro roots on aluminum toxic soil.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** by Planters Products, Inc. (50.59 percent CaO), **Macrock Limestone** by Donumdei 1 Corp. (36 to 42 percent calcium), **Calcic Lime** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (35.52 percent calcium) and **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soils ahead of planting.
Magnesium deficiency in taro

Older leaf blades yellow between the veins while the veins stay dark green. As it gets worse the margins and the spaces between veins turn brown and die, leaves may curl and drop early. You see it most at this stage: mid season.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in gabi
Sandy soils, acid soils and heavy potash.
How to tell it apart
Potassium deficiency scorches margins without the clear green vein pattern. To be sure, leaf test (below 0.2 percent magnesium is deficient, CTAHR).
What to apply for magnesium deficiency
Give about 80 kg magnesium sulfate per hectare (32 kg per acre) in bands near the plants. Do not apply it together with potash. Use Dolomite on acid soils.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soils with dolomite.
Sulfur deficiency in taro

Roots and shoots grow less, leaf blades are smaller, and the younger leaves turn evenly yellow. The yellow is uniform across the blade, without a pattern of green veins. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why sulfur deficiency happens in gabi
Soils low in organic matter and burning crop waste.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen deficiency yellows the old leaves first. To be sure, leaf test (below 0.2 percent sulfur is deficient, CTAHR).
What to apply for sulfur deficiency
Use Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 or single superphosphate. Give about 25 kg sulfur dust per hectare on sulfur poor soils, or Gypsum on alkaline soils.

Sold here with sulfur: **Farmfix Sulfur** by Philippine FarmFix, Inc. (99 percent sulfur), **VSI Sulfur Powder** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (99.5 percent sulfur), **Atlas Ammosul** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (21 0 0 with 24 percent sulfur) and **Philphos 21 0 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (21 0 0 (ammonium sulfate)). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [ammonium sulfate fertilizer](/blog/ammonium-sulfate-21-0-0), and the page on [sulfur deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/sulfur-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add organic matter.
Iron deficiency in taro
Younger leaf blades first yellow between the veins, then turn evenly bleached. Fewer side roots form. You see it most at this stage: early growth, in upland taro.
Why iron deficiency happens in gabi
Upland (not flooded) soils with high pH. Flooding makes iron more available.
How to tell it apart

Manganese toxicity on older leaves looks like iron deficiency but starts on the old blades. Manganese deficiency also starts on young leaves. To be sure, leaf test of leaf number 2 (below 100 ppm iron is deficient, CTAHR).
What to apply for iron deficiency
Give about 15 kg ferrous sulfate per hectare (6 kg per acre) to the soil, following a soil test.

Sold here with iron: **Ferrous Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Cleveland Industries Inc. (20 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulfate Monohydrate** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (30 percent iron), **Grow More Liquid Chelate Iron with Sulfur** by Sagrex Corporation (5 percent iron and 3 percent sulfur) and **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [iron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/iron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep organic matter high in upland taro fields.
Zinc deficiency in taro
Taro short of zinc is stunted in roots and shoots, but CTAHR saw no other clear signs. Smaller, distorted young leaves in a rosette and slow leaf growth. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why zinc deficiency happens in gabi
Soils outside pH 5 to 7.5 and heavy phosphorus.
How to tell it apart
Many problems stunt taro. Only a leaf test confirms zinc. To be sure, leaf test (20 to 40 ppm zinc is sufficient, CTAHR).
What to apply for zinc deficiency
Give about 20 kg Zinc sulfate per hectare (8 kg per acre) to the soil, or a spray of 2 g zinc sulfate with 2.5 g lime per liter in severe cases. Keep zinc and phosphate applications apart.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, test before adding zinc.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any taro nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your gabi needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Taro nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my gabi leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: older leaf blades yellow first, then all of them, with stunted plants and few suckers. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at calcium deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in taro?
items.a: Apply nitrogen following the soil test, for example Urea 46 0 0 or Complete 14 14 14 in split doses. You can also give a urea spray of 10 g per liter every 15 days.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in taro?
items.a: Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 following the soil test, split in parts. Give a potassium sulfate spray of 10 g per liter as a quick fix.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in taro?
items.a: Use single superphosphate for a quick fix and rock phosphate for the long term, following the soil test.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my gabi lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the taro nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
